Italy became a kingdom in 1861, but Rome and Venice weren't in it yet. The map shows each piece joining, and what it cost.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ The starting point is the Kingdom of Sardinia, ruled from Turin by the House of Savoy. Prime Minister Cavour wanted Austria out of northern Italy and found an ally in Napoleon III of France.
2/ 1859: France and Sardinia beat Austria at Magenta and Solferino, and Sardinia took Lombardy. In March 1860 it also annexed Tuscany, Parma, Modena and the Papal Legations.
3/ The price: on 24 March 1860 Sardinia ceded Savoy and Nice to France under the Treaty of Turin. That's the 'ceded to France' corner on the map. Garibaldi was born in Nice and resented the deal.

4/ May 1860: Garibaldi's volunteers, the Thousand, won at Calatafimi in Sicily on 13 May. He took the island, crossed to the mainland and toppled the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies. That's the huge '1860' block.
5/ On 17 March 1861 the first Italian parliament, meeting in Turin, proclaimed Victor Emmanuel II King of Italy. Rome was declared the capital ten days later, though it was still outside the kingdom.

6/ 1866: Italy allied with Prussia against Austria and got Venetia, even though it lost on land at Custoza. 1870: French troops had left Rome, and Italian soldiers breached its walls at Porta Pia on 20 September.
7/ Unification took from 1859 to 1870, yet 17 March 1861 is the date celebrated. Was Italy made by Garibaldi's volunteers or Cavour's diplomacy? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
